newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals spiral lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals spiral lower, led by gold.

text.p: The precious metals sank to new nadirs in European trading on Wednesday, dragged lower by the wake of the overwhelmingly bearish gold market.
Silver fixed a fresh 20-month lows, while platinum and palladium fixed at the lowest levels since 1993.
Gold, which has shed some $10 in a month, fixed marginally firmer at $373.95 an ounce, after sinking on Tuesday to fix at a two-year low of $373.50.
But dealers and analysts said gold threatened to plummet further in the near term amid fresh fears of future gold sales by European central banks.

"The market is so bearish right now, there's got to be a realistic chance of a further shake out. My one note of succour to the bulls is that at the moment the market is seeing nothing but bad news," said analyst Rhona O'Connell of T. Hoare and Co.
Last week, comments from a director of the Swiss National Bank (SNB) that the SNB may eventually take a more pro-active approach to its gold reserves, cast a further pall.
Uncertainty over gold's future role in European Monetary Union was also unnerving the bullion market, dealers said.
"People think that gold is not going to play a big role, in which case $350 here we come," a dealer said.
More immediately, reported forward selling by gold mining houses in South Africa and Australia was depressing prices.
Soaring stock markets were continuing to discourage investors from putting money into the precious metals.

"You've got producers panic selling on the way down. And money is also flowing out of metals and into the equity markets. With the Dow where it is, no one cares a whit for metals," a London-based bullion dealer noted.
Demand, although in theory at its annual peak, was not big enough to counteract the downward pressure.
The rest of the precious metals -- silver, platinum and palladium -- have become casualties of gold's weakness.
"There's nothing fundamental pushing platinum and palladium lower. They're just being sucked down by the bearish sentiment surrounding gold," a London-based dealer said.
Earlier platinum fixed at $377.75 an ounce, its lowest level since December 8, 1993, while palladium fixed at $114.75, the lowest since April 20 of the same year.
Silver slipped to fix at $4.74 an ounce, the lowest fixing since March 29, 1995.
